places.name: Zakouma National Park
places.what: A national park established in 1963 in south-eastern Chad, covering about 3,054 km2. Poaching decimated its elephants between 2002 and 2010, and since African Parks took over management in 2010 the herd has recovered.

notNotFound: Chad's INSEED site (inseed.td) is JavaScript-only and its PDFs return an HTML page, so the RGPH2 report could not be read; the population figure comes from a 2012 thematic synthesis citing INSEED. Other publications give 951,418 or 963,657 for the same 2009 census, which could not be reconciled.
The INSEED catalogue (anad.inseed.td) lists 963,657 for 'Ville de N'Djamena' but only as a variable category, so it was not recorded as the main value.
UNESCO World Heritage Centre pages return 403: Lakes of Ounianga facts come from Explore Chad (institutional tourism site) and a peer-reviewed article.
Zakouma area/elephant figures differ between sources; the current elephant count (c. 550-800) was not recorded.

Place de la Nation: no source found for its construction date or design; a 2026 article on a new monument on a 'place de l'Indépendance' near the presidential palace was not recorded because it is unclear whether it is the same site.
No readable independent source found for the Grand Mosque's exact opening year (1970s) or size, and none for the Grand Marché's history beyond its local name.
Wikipedia-derived pages and Persée paper on the Grand Marché (1978, abstract only) not usable for facts.
